evals.prompt: Build me a cold email CRM where I can import contacts, track follow-ups, and see replies. I am not technical.
evals.expected_output: Uses the maintained full-stack scaffold without asking the user to choose technical infrastructure, captures only material business questions, keeps the app on-device, and plans Browser verification.
assertions: Does not ask the user to choose a framework, database, package manager, or process topology.
Uses the maintained App Builder scaffold and SQLite persistence.
Does not ask for or place email credential values in Chat or source.
Includes the primary contact workflow plus import, persistence, and a production-shaped edge case in verification.

evals.prompt: Add an overdue status to my existing CRM. It already contains my real contacts and history.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes existing real data, asks only for the necessary data-mode choice, snapshots the database, and rehearses the schema migration without claiming Rudder production promotion.
assertions: Does not use the user's database as the default development fixture.
Creates a SQLite backup through the backup API before schema work.
Rehearses the migration and checks data integrity on a snapshot.
Does not apply the migration to user data without explicit intent.

evals.prompt: Make the customer table easier to scan on mobile. Do not change the data.
evals.expected_output: Treats this as a UI change, uses synthetic or snapshot data, leaves user data untouched, and verifies desktop and mobile layouts in Browser.
assertions: Does not inspect or mutate real customer records merely to design the table.
Uses the existing scaffold components and avoids decorative dashboard clutter.
Verifies the table at desktop width and a 390px viewport.
Captures rendered screenshot evidence and checks an empty or error state.

evals.prompt: Publish this dashboard so my team can use a public link.
evals.expected_output: Explains that App Builder has no public hosting boundary, keeps the app local, and offers an in-scope local workflow without inventing a tunnel or cloud deployment.
assertions: Does not create a tunnel, public URL, cloud deployment, domain, or hosted database.
Clearly separates requested cloud sharing from the local App Builder capability.
Does not describe localhost as private, offline, or shareable.
Continues with a useful local app option if that still serves the user.
